root.name: Alekhine Defense: Exchange Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 Nf6 2. e5 Nd5 3. d4 d6 4. c4 Nb6 5. exd6

overview: White trades the e5 pawn for Black's d-pawn, giving up the big space grab for a simpler game with a c4/d4 centre. Black recaptures with ...cxd6 or ...exd6 and then plays ...g6, ...Bg7 and ...O-O or ...Nc6, developing against White's centre. White has a small space edge and Black has few weaknesses, leading to calm positional play.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nc3, Be3, Rc1 and Nf3 against a central pawn mass with c4 and d4
Keep a small space edge and use the c4/d4 duo with a Maroczy-like feel

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with ...g6 and ...Bg7, ...O-O, and counter with ...Nc6 or ...Bg4 and ...e5
Use the half-open c-file after ...cxd6 or play a flexible ...exd6 structure

typical_structures.structure: White c4/d4 against Black d6 with ...g6 fianchetto; cxd6 gives Black a half-open c-file

character.notes: Simplified, positional play with no early forcing lines; Black has few weaknesses.

structure.notes: After ...cxd6 Black has a half-open c-file and White has c4/d4; semi-open.

approach.notes: A regular option at all levels.

level.notes: Plans are understood positionally, little memorisation.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5...exd6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black gets a symmetric structure without the c-file and a solid set-up.

character.reason: A quieter line than Four Pawns, neither sharp nor rock-solid.

structure.reason: After ...cxd6 Black has a half-open c-file against the c4/d4 centre.

approach.reason: A regular line in the Alekhine.

level.reason: Positional plans matter more than theory.

plans.reason: White's space and Black's c-file counterplay define the middlegame.
